songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy ’71 show with scorching guitar and tight rhythm
ai_show_review.blurb: The set shines with a guitar‑forward mix as Jerry tears through Good Lovin' and Loser, while Phil’s bass bombs drive the second half. Highlights include Cumberland Blues, China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, Sugar Magnolia and an explosive In The Midnight Hour. The soundboard capture is clear overall, though vocals sit low and there are brief drop‑outs.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at East Hall on April 10 1971 finds the Dead locked in a high‑octane groove that feels as fresh today as it did back then. Jerry’s guitar is turned up to eleven, carving soaring leads on Good Lovin' and ripping through the Loser solo, while his tone dominates the board mix. Phil lays down thunderous bass bombs that propel the second set into sustained intensity, especially during Cumberland Blues and Sugar Magnolia. Bob locks in with crisp rhythm chops, adding a solid backbone to the China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition. Billy’s drumming provides a funky undercurrent, even if it sits low in the mix, and Pigpen’s keyboards sit mostly in the background on this recording. The set closes with a fiery In The Midnight Hour that showcases the band’s collective tightness. Though the board is guitar‑forward and suffers occasional drop‑outs on Truckin', the overall clarity lets listeners enjoy every improvisational spark of this high‑energy early‑’70s performance.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture that preserves the guitar‑forward mix and high energy of the night, with only minor drop‑outs.
